result.title: PseuDRAGON: Knowledge-Guided Local LLMs for Financial-Data Pseudonymization in Closed Networks
result.comment: 8 pages, 3 figures. Accepted as a full paper in the AI for Intelligent Financial Technologies (AIFT) track of the 42nd ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing (SAC 2027). Gwangui Hong and Seonho An contributed equally
result.summary: Staff pseudonymizing financial data in closed networks must interpret abbreviated column names, identify personal information, and choose processing methods. Local language models can assist, but may give different labels for the same input. PseuDRAGON keeps confirmed judgments and corrections outside a fixed model and reuses them through exact-name lookup and learned rules. For expert review, the workflow searches institutional policy, national privacy law, then international sources. Across 92 columns from one institution, rules increase reuse under the same approval checks from 75 to 83 labels without reuse errors when all training judgments are available. With 25% of the training judgments, withholding non-PII rules for unseen names eliminated the extra PII misses in replay at the cost of lower reuse. Revising or withdrawing approvals rebuilds derived rules, and tests on synthetic records verify that selected methods produce the specified outputs. In three paired runs, the history-first baseline cut automated identification time by 83.0% on average versus no reuse.

AI.brief_summary: 面向封闭网络中员工对金融数据脱敏的需求，提出 PseuDRAGON：把已确认的判断与纠正保存在固定模型之外，通过列名精确查找和学习规则复用，并按机构政策、国家隐私法、国际来源的顺序检索以支持专家复核。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将判断外置为可复用规则、并显式规定证据检索顺序与审批重建的机制，可能与 LVR 中「何时依赖内部状态、何时检索外部证据及停止」的问题表述相通，但属较远领域，仅供核查，未见与视觉推理的直接联系。
